name: Elizabeth Yoon
life: “I stopped sleeping in doorways when a woman offered me her spare key and a time to return it.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Elizabeth often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I used to hide my key in a shoe. After losing my home I hate the idea somebody else carries it.
appearance: Elizabeth has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Elizabeth counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Elizabeth loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Elizabeth remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To recover control over access to the home.
family: Hana Solberg is Elizabeth’s second cousin. Elizabeth sets the time to leave. Hana picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The last green*, Hana says, “The best view is from the passenger side at the crest.”
connections: Rae Meyer. They agree which doors will open for a volunteer and which owners will open themselves.
